grammar.title: The Passive: All Tenses and Passive Infinitive
grammar.explanation:
The passive **moves the receiver of the action to the front of the sentence**. Form it with **be + past participle**: *The deposit was placed in escrow.*

Use the passive **when the doer is unknown, obvious, or unimportant**. *Ticket prices are kept high by the oligopoly* puts the focus on the prices, not on who keeps them high.

The passive **works in every tense**. *The old network was controlled by a monopoly* is past simple, and *the valley has been restored* is present perfect.

*That wistful smile will never be forgotten* is the future passive. **Only the verb be changes**; the past participle stays the same.

**Reporting verbs** pair the passive with an infinitive. *The imperious manager is said to have alienated the team* means that people say he did.

A common mistake is **dropping the past participle ending**. Say *was placed* and *are kept*, never *was place* or *are keep*.
examples: "The deposit *was placed in **escrow*** before the inspection began." (past simple passive: the deposit received the action)
"The old network *was controlled by a **monopoly*** for thirty years." (past simple passive with the agent named)
"Ticket prices *are kept* artificially high by the ***oligopoly***." (present simple passive for a general truth)
"The wetlands *have been restored* through careful **conservation**." (present perfect passive: a finished action with a present result)
"The *imperious* manager *is said to have alienated* the whole team." (passive reporting verb + perfect infinitive)

practice.q: Complete: The deposit ___ in escrow before the inspection. (was placed / placed)
practice.a: was placed. Say: The deposit was placed in escrow.

practice.q: Complete: Ticket prices ___ high by the oligopoly. (are kept / keep)
practice.a: are kept. Say: Ticket prices are kept high by the oligopoly.

practice.q: Fix the mistake: *The valley has restored by conservation.*
practice.a: The valley has been restored by conservation. The valley receives the action, so the passive is required.

practice.q: Complete: The imperious manager ___ to have alienated the team. (is said / says)
practice.a: is said. Say: The imperious manager is said to have alienated the team.
